models_evaluated: state-of-the-art object detection models for human sperm

links.outcome: Model precision and recall across clinics and imaging conditions after training on diverse multi-condition data
links.effect: Rich training dataset yielded ICC 0.97 (95% CI 0.94-0.99) for precision and 0.97 (0.93-0.99) for recall; multi-center validation showed no significant differences in precision or recall across clinics.
links.quote: Multi-center clinical validation showed no significant differences in model precision or recall across different clinics and applications.

links.outcome: Generalizability of detection model to new samples and external clinics after enriching training data
links.effect: Internal blind tests and external multi-center validation showed ICC of 0.97 for precision and recall, with no significant differences across clinics.
links.quote: The results validated the hypothesis that the richness of data in the training dataset is a key factor impacting model generalizability.

unlisted_practices: Enriching training data with diverse imaging magnifications, modes, and sample preprocessing conditions to improve cross-clinic generalizability
Ablation studies to identify imaging factors driving performance drops

screen.reason: The study directly tests how enriching training data with multi-center/variable imaging conditions versus standard datasets safeguards model generalizability and cross-clinic transfer.
